sec: Boston method: normal values, valid ABG and step 1 · p827

items.q: Match the Boston method normal values — 1) pH  2) pCO₂  3) HCO₃⁻ … A) 40 mmHg  B) 24 mEq/L  C) 7.4
items.exp: Boston normal values: pH 7.4, pCO₂ 40 mmHg and HCO₃⁻ 24 mEq/L. (Book p827)
The Boston method uses [H⁺] = 24 × PaCO₂/HCO₃⁻, rearranged as [HCO₃⁻] = 24 × PaCO₂/H⁺. (Book p827)
The second printed form of the Boston relation is [HCO₃⁻] = 24 × PaCO₂/H⁺. (Book p827)

items.q: To be a valid ABG, the calculated [HCO₃⁻] should match the venous blood [HCO₃⁻] within:
items.exp: Valid ABG: calculated [HCO₃⁻] = ±2 mEq of [HCO₃⁻] in a venous blood sample. (Book p827)

items.q: An ABG reports a calculated HCO₃⁻ of 24 mEq/L while the venous sample gives 28 mEq/L. Is the gas valid?
opts: No — the difference of 4 mEq/L exceeds the accepted ±2 mEq limit
Yes — any difference under 5 mEq/L is acceptable
Yes — the venous sample is the less reliable of the two
No — a valid ABG requires identical values in both samples
items.exp: Validity requires the calculated [HCO₃⁻] to be within ±2 mEq of the venous blood [HCO₃⁻]. (Book p827)

items.q: Match step 1 of interpretation — 1) pH < 7.4  2) pH > 7.4  3) Normal pH of the Boston method … A) 7.4  B) Alkalosis  C) Acidosis
items.exp: Step 1: a pH below 7.4 is acidosis and a pH above 7.4 is alkalosis. (Book p827)

items.q: According to step 1 of the Boston method, the pH cut-off used to separate acidosis from alkalosis is:
items.exp: Step 1 uses 7.4 as the cut-off (< 7.4 acidosis, > 7.4 alkalosis), the Boston method's normal pH. (Book p827)

items.q: All but one of these belong to the Boston method's normal values and validity rules. Which is the odd one out?
opts: A valid ABG requires arterial blood only, with no venous comparison
Calculated HCO₃⁻ within ±2 mEq of the venous sample
items.exp: Validity is defined by comparing the calculated [HCO₃⁻] with the [HCO₃⁻] of a venous blood sample (±2 mEq), so a venous comparison is explicitly required. (Book p827)

items.q: ‘Step 1 of the Boston method uses pH to decide whether the primary problem is an acidosis or an alkalosis.’
opts: True — pH < 7.4 is acidosis and pH > 7.4 is alkalosis
False — step 1 uses PaCO₂ to decide the primary problem
False — step 1 uses the anion gap to decide the primary problem
True, but the cut-off for step 1 is pH 7.36
